stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether nausea after a new taste produces an aversion to that taste. They recruited 40 laboratory rats and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Rats in one condition drank sweetened water and were then given an injection that causes mild nausea. Rats in the other condition drank sweetened water and were then given a harmless salt-water injection. The researchers then recorded the volume in milliliters of sweetened water that each rat drank the next day. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.01.

rows.group: The group given the nausea-causing injection
The group given the salt-water injection

stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether a new drug reduces anxiety. They recruited 150 adults diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition took the new drug every day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition took a placebo pill that looked identical every day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard anxiety questionnaire after eight weeks.

Researchers collected data from 600 university students. For each one, they recorded conscientiousness score on a personality inventory and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.35.

Researchers investigated whether a smiling expression makes cartoons seem funnier. They recruited 90 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a pen between their teeth, which produces a smile. Participants in the other condition held a pen between their lips, which prevents a smile. The researchers then recorded the rating from 1 to 10 that each participant gave to a set of cartoons.

Researchers collected data from 350 adults. For each one, they recorded the number of stressful life events in the past year and the number of colds in the past year. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.33.

Researchers investigated whether mindfulness meditation lowers stress. They recruited 84 office workers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition practiced mindfulness meditation for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition listened to an audiobook for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded the level of the stress hormone cortisol in a saliva sample from each participant.
Researchers collected data from 300 fifth-grade students. For each one, they recorded working memory span and reading comprehension score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.52.

Researchers investigated whether the color of a drink affects the ability to identify its flavor. They recruited 70 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition tasted ten fruit drinks whose colors did not match their flavors. Participants in the other condition tasted the same ten drinks with matching colors. The researchers then recorded the number of flavors out of ten that each participant named correctly.

Researchers investigated whether a phone conversation reduces what drivers notice. They recruited 64 licensed drivers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a hands-free phone conversation while using a driving simulator. Participants in the other condition used the driving simulator without a phone. The researchers then recorded the number of road signs out of 30 that each participant failed to notice.

Researchers investigated whether keeping a gratitude journal raises well-being. They recruited 110 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition wrote down three things they were grateful for every night for a month. Participants in the other condition wrote down three things they had done every night for a month. The researchers then recorded each participant's rating of life satisfaction on a scale from 1 to 10 at the end of the month.

Researchers investigated whether praise increases hand raising in class. They recruited 50 second-grade students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were praised by the teacher each time they raised a hand before speaking. Children in the other condition received no special response when they raised a hand. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child raised a hand during one week.

Researchers collected data from 400 high school students. For each one, they recorded the average number of hours slept per night and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.45.

Researchers investigated whether agreeing to a small request makes people more likely to agree to a large one. They recruited 120 homeowners and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Homeowners in one condition were first asked to sign a road-safety petition and two weeks later were asked to put a large sign in their garden. Homeowners in the other condition were only asked to put the large sign in their garden. The researchers then recorded the percentage of homeowners in each group who agreed to display the sign.

Researchers investigated whether guided hints help children learn to solve puzzles. They recruited 64 five-year-old children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition solved practice puzzles with hints from an adult that were gradually reduced. Children in the other condition solved the same practice puzzles alone. The researchers then recorded the number of new puzzles out of ten that each child later solved without help.
Researchers collected data from 500 adults aged 20 to 80. For each one, they recorded age and score on a timed reasoning test. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.55.
Researchers collected data from 450 adults. For each one, they recorded optimism score and the number of days of illness in a year. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.30.

Researchers investigated whether an expected reward reduces children's later interest in drawing. They recruited 60 preschool children who enjoyed drawing and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were promised a certificate for drawing and received it. Children in the other condition drew with no reward mentioned. The researchers then recorded the number of minutes that each child chose to spend drawing during free time one week later.

Researchers investigated whether caffeine improves attention. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition drank coffee containing 200 milligrams of caffeine. Participants in the other condition drank decaffeinated coffee that tasted the same. The researchers then recorded the number of targets that each participant correctly detected in a ten-minute computer task.

Researchers investigated whether spreading study sessions out improves long-term retention. They recruited 90 high school students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition studied a list of 40 words in six ten-minute sessions on six different days. Participants in the other condition studied the same list in a single sixty-minute session. The researchers then recorded the number of words out of 40 that each participant recalled on a test one month later.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether cognitive-behavioral therapy reduces depression. They hypothesized that the treatment would affect the severity of depression.

**Participants.** The sample was 90 adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder, recruited from one city. All participants gave informed consent, were told they could withdraw at any time, and were debriefed afterward. The plan was approved by an institutional review board.

**Method.** The participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition received twelve weekly sessions of cognitive-behavioral therapy. Participants in the other condition were placed on a waiting list for twelve weeks and were treated afterward. The researchers recorded each participant's score on a standard depression questionnaire after twelve weeks.

**Results.** The group that received therapy: mean depression score = 11. The group on the waiting list: mean depression score = 21. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **How does long-term stress affect health, and what reduces its effects?**

**Source A.** In a study of 350 adults, the number of stressful life events in the past year correlated with the number of colds in that year (r = +0.33). Adults who reported sleeping less tended to report both more stress and more colds.

**Source B.** In an experiment, 84 office workers were randomly assigned to practice mindfulness meditation or to listen to an audiobook for twenty minutes a day. After eight weeks, the meditation group had a mean cortisol level of 9.8 nmol/L and the audiobook group 13.5 nmol/L (p = 0.02).

**Source C.** Researchers followed 500 people for a year after a major flood. Those who reported strong support from family and friends had fewer symptoms of illness and depression than those who reported little support.

questions.stem: Before collecting any data, a researcher must have her plan approved by a university committee that checks its ethics. What is this committee called?

options.why: Debriefing is the explaining of a study's purpose, and any deception, to participants after it ends.
Informed consent is the agreement of participants to take part after they have been told what a study involves.
Confidentiality is the keeping private of participants' identities and data.
Correct. An institutional review board is the committee that reviews research plans to make sure participants are treated ethically.

questions.explanation: An institutional review board is the committee that reviews research plans to make sure participants are treated ethically.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a supertaster?

options.text: A chemical signal released by one member of a species that affects the behavior of others
options.why: That describes a pheromone.

options.text: The sense of smell, the only sense that does not pass through the thalamus first
options.why: That describes olfaction.

options.text: A person with more taste receptors than average, who experiences tastes more intensely
options.why: Correct. This is what a supertaster means.

options.text: The sense of taste, which detects sweet, sour, salty, bitter, umami and oleogustus
options.why: That describes gustation.

questions.explanation: A supertaster is a person with more taste receptors than average, who experiences tastes more intensely.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The two groups had the same average result
options.why: The table shows different averages.

options.text: The results prove that every individual in the first group differed from every individual in the second
options.why: The table reports group averages, not individual scores.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant, so it is unlikely to be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

options.text: The difference between the groups is probably due to chance
options.why: A p value of 0.01 is below 0.05, so chance is an unlikely explanation.

questions.explanation: A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the participants to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that the results could be generalized to the whole population
options.why: That is the purpose of random sampling, not random assignment.

options.text: So that the study would have more participants
options.why: Random assignment does not change the sample size.

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable
options.why: Correct. Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

options.text: So that nobody would know the hypothesis
options.why: That describes a blind procedure.

questions.explanation: Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.stem: An eighty-year-old reflects on her life and feels that it was meaningful and well lived. Which of Erikson's stages is this?

options.why: Intimacy versus isolation is Erikson's stage in young adulthood, in which people seek close, lasting relationships.
Correct. Integrity versus despair is Erikson's stage in late adulthood, in which people look back on life with satisfaction or regret.
Identity versus role confusion is Erikson's stage in adolescence, in which teenagers work out who they are.
Generativity versus stagnation is Erikson's stage in middle adulthood, in which people seek to contribute to the world through family and work.

questions.explanation: Integrity versus despair is Erikson's stage in late adulthood, in which people look back on life with satisfaction or regret.

questions.stem: After a large, relaxed dinner, Ana's body directs energy toward digestion and her breathing slows. Which part of the nervous system is most active?

options.why: The central nervous system is the brain and spinal cord.
The somatic nervous system is the division of the peripheral nervous system that controls voluntary movement of the skeletal muscles.
Correct. The parasympathetic nervous system is the division of the autonomic nervous system that calms the body and conserves energy.
The autonomic nervous system is the division of the peripheral nervous system that controls glands and internal organs without conscious effort.

questions.explanation: The parasympathetic nervous system is the division of the autonomic nervous system that calms the body and conserves energy.

questions.stem: Lights on a sign flash one after another, and viewers see a single light moving along the sign. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Color constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same color under different lighting.
Correct. Apparent movement is the perception of motion when a series of still images or lights is shown in quick succession.
Size constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same size even when its image on the retina changes.
Shape constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same shape even when the viewing angle changes.

questions.explanation: Apparent movement is the perception of motion when a series of still images or lights is shown in quick succession.

questions.stem: Although her son failed the exam, a mother makes clear that she values and accepts him just the same. In humanistic theory, this is which of the following?

options.why: The self-actualizing tendency is in humanistic theory, the inborn drive of people to grow and fulfill their potential.
The unconscious is in psychodynamic theory, the store of thoughts, wishes and memories that a person is not aware of but that still influences behavior.
Correct. Unconditional positive regard is the attitude of total acceptance toward another person, whatever they say or do.
A defense mechanism is in psychodynamic theory, a method the ego uses without awareness to reduce anxiety by distorting reality.

questions.explanation: Unconditional positive regard is the attitude of total acceptance toward another person, whatever they say or do.

questions.stem: In a drug trial, neither the patients nor the doctors who assess them know who is receiving the drug. Which procedure is this?

options.why: Statistical significance is the conclusion that a result is unlikely to have occurred by chance, usually when p is below 0.05.
Effect size is the measure of how large the difference or relationship found in a study is.
Correct. A double-blind procedure is a procedure in which neither the participants nor the researchers who deal with them know who is in which condition.
The control group is the group in an experiment that does not receive the treatment and is used for comparison.

questions.explanation: A double-blind procedure is a procedure in which neither the participants nor the researchers who deal with them know who is in which condition.

questions.stem: Critics argue that a so-called creativity test actually measures vocabulary. Which quality are they questioning?

options.why: Split-half reliability is the consistency of scores between two halves of the same test.
Correct. Construct validity is the extent to which a test measures the concept it claims to measure.
Predictive validity is the extent to which test scores forecast the future performance they are meant to predict.
Test-retest reliability is the consistency of scores when the same people take the same test twice.

questions.explanation: Construct validity is the extent to which a test measures the concept it claims to measure.

questions.stem: A tourist calls another country's eating customs 'wrong' because they differ from the customs at home. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Prejudice is an unjustified negative attitude toward a group and its members.
A stereotype is a generalized belief about a group of people.
Correct. Ethnocentrism is the tendency to judge other cultures by the standards of one's own culture.
The just-world phenomenon is the tendency to believe that people get what they deserve.

questions.explanation: Ethnocentrism is the tendency to judge other cultures by the standards of one's own culture.

questions.stem: A day after meeting twelve new people, Joy remembers only the names of the first two she met. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The recency effect is the tendency to remember the last items in a list well.
The serial position effect is the tendency to remember the first and last items in a list better than the middle ones.
The spacing effect is the finding that study spread over time produces better long-term memory than study crammed together.
Correct. The primacy effect is the tendency to remember the first items in a list well.

questions.explanation: The primacy effect is the tendency to remember the first items in a list well.

questions.stem: A second study of a different pair of measures finds r = −0.55. Which relationship is stronger?

options.text: The relationship in the first study, because its coefficient is closer to zero
options.why: A coefficient closer to zero shows a weaker relationship.

options.text: The relationship with the positive sign, whatever its size
options.why: The sign shows direction, not strength.

options.text: The relationship in the second study, because its coefficient is farther from zero
options.why: Correct. The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

options.text: Neither, because relationships with different signs cannot be compared
options.why: Strength can be compared by distance from zero.

questions.explanation: The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.stem: The group that held the pen between the teeth rated the cartoons as funnier. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: The facial expression produced by holding a pen caused the difference in amusement
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

options.text: The facial expression produced by holding a pen and amusement are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the technique of echoing, restating and seeking clarification of what the client says?

options.why: Correct. Active listening is the technique of echoing, restating and seeking clarification of what the client says.
Free association is the psychodynamic technique in which the client says whatever comes to mind.
Hypnosis is a state of heightened suggestibility that can help reduce pain and anxiety but does not reliably recover memories.
Group therapy is the therapy in which several clients meet together with a therapist and benefit from each other's support.

questions.explanation: Active listening is the technique of echoing, restating and seeking clarification of what the client says.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the directionality problem in this study?

options.text: It is unclear whether the correlation is positive or negative
options.why: The sign of r shows the direction of the relationship.

options.text: It is unclear how many people took part
options.why: The sample size is stated.

options.text: It is unclear whether the two measures were recorded
options.why: Both measures were recorded.

options.text: It is unclear whether the first measure influences the second or the second influences the first
options.why: Correct. A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

questions.explanation: A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the therapy that teaches skills for tolerating distress and controlling emotions, often used for borderline personality disorder?

options.why: Correct. Dialectical behavior therapy is the therapy that teaches skills for tolerating distress and controlling emotions, often used for borderline personality disorder.
Cognitive-behavioral therapy is the therapy that combines changing self-defeating thoughts with changing behavior.
The cognitive triad is the pattern of negative thoughts about oneself, the world and the future that is found in depression.
Rational emotive behavior therapy is the confrontational cognitive therapy, developed by Ellis, that actively challenges a client's irrational beliefs.

questions.explanation: Dialectical behavior therapy is the therapy that teaches skills for tolerating distress and controlling emotions, often used for borderline personality disorder.

questions.stem: Too little of one neurotransmitter is linked to the tremors of Parkinson's disease, and too much activity of it is linked to schizophrenia. Which neurotransmitter is this?

options.why: Correct. Dopamine is the neurotransmitter that influences movement, attention, and feelings of reward.
Glutamate is the brain's main excitatory neurotransmitter, which is involved in memory.
Norepinephrine is the neurotransmitter that helps control alertness and arousal.
Serotonin is the neurotransmitter that affects mood, hunger and sleep.

questions.explanation: Dopamine is the neurotransmitter that influences movement, attention, and feelings of reward.

questions.stem: A child's schooling is disrupted by a pandemic at age eight. In ecological systems theory, the timing of this event is part of which system?

options.why: Correct. The chronosystem is in ecological systems theory, the life stage and historical events that affect a child.
The mesosystem is in ecological systems theory, the relationships between the groups in a child's immediate surroundings.
The macrosystem is in ecological systems theory, the cultural values, laws and customs that surround a child.
The exosystem is in ecological systems theory, the settings that affect a child indirectly, such as a parent's workplace.

questions.explanation: The chronosystem is in ecological systems theory, the life stage and historical events that affect a child.

questions.stem: Omar generally feels that he is a valuable and likeable person. Which term describes this overall feeling?

options.why: A personality inventory is a questionnaire with many true-false or agree-disagree items that measures a range of traits.
Self-concept is all the thoughts and feelings a person has in answer to the question 'Who am I?'.
Reciprocal determinism is the idea that a person's behavior, thoughts and environment all influence one another.
Correct. Self-esteem is a person's overall feeling of self-worth.

questions.explanation: Self-esteem is a person's overall feeling of self-worth.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the structure that forms new explicit memories of facts and events?

options.why: The corpus callosum is the band of fibers that connects the two hemispheres of the brain.
Correct. The hippocampus is the structure that forms new explicit memories of facts and events.
The cerebral cortex is the wrinkled outer layer of the brain, which handles thinking, perception and voluntary movement.
The amygdala is the structure that processes fear and aggression.

questions.explanation: The hippocampus is the structure that forms new explicit memories of facts and events.

questions.stem: Grandpa tells detailed stories about his wedding day and his first job. Which kind of memory is he drawing on?

options.why: Elaborative rehearsal is the linking of new information to existing knowledge and meaning to store it in long-term memory.
Correct. Autobiographical memory is the memory of the events of one's own life.
Maintenance rehearsal is the repeating of information over and over to keep it in short-term memory.
Highly superior autobiographical memory is the rare ability to recall almost every day of one's life in detail.

questions.explanation: Autobiographical memory is the memory of the events of one's own life.

questions.stem: A psychologist says a client's anxiety comes from unresolved childhood conflicts that the client is not aware of. Which perspective is this?

options.why: The sociocultural perspective is the view that disorders result from social and cultural factors, such as poverty and discrimination.
The biological perspective is the view that disorders result from genetic, brain or chemical causes.
The cognitive perspective is the view that disorders result from distorted or irrational ways of thinking.
Correct. The psychodynamic perspective is the view that disorders result from unconscious conflicts, often rooted in childhood.

questions.explanation: The psychodynamic perspective is the view that disorders result from unconscious conflicts, often rooted in childhood.

questions.stem: To treat a child's fear of rabbits, a therapist gives the child a favorite snack while a rabbit is slowly brought closer. Which technique is this?

options.why: Habituation is the decrease in response to a stimulus that is presented over and over.
A taste aversion is a learned dislike of a food that was followed by illness.
Correct. Counterconditioning is the replacing of an unwanted response to a stimulus with a new response, by pairing the stimulus with something pleasant.
One-trial conditioning is learning that happens after a single pairing of two stimuli.

questions.explanation: Counterconditioning is the replacing of an unwanted response to a stimulus with a new response, by pairing the stimulus with something pleasant.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes deviation from the social norm?

options.text: The negative attitudes and discrimination directed at people who have a psychological disorder
options.why: That describes stigma.

options.text: The criterion for a disorder that the behavior causes suffering to the person
options.why: That describes distress.

options.text: The criterion for a disorder that the behavior differs markedly from what a culture expects
options.why: Correct. This is what deviation from the social norm means.

options.text: The criterion for a disorder that the behavior interferes with daily life, such as work and relationships
options.why: That describes dysfunction.

questions.explanation: Deviation from the social norm is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior differs markedly from what a culture expects.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes secondary sex characteristics?

options.text: The nonreproductive traits of sexual maturity, such as body hair and a deeper voice
options.why: Correct. This is what secondary sex characteristics means.

options.text: The body structures, such as ovaries and testes, that make reproduction possible
options.why: That describes primary sex characteristics.
That describes menarche.

options.text: The natural end of menstruation and of the ability to reproduce, usually around age 50
options.why: That describes menopause.

questions.explanation: Secondary sex characteristics is the nonreproductive traits of sexual maturity, such as body hair and a deeper voice.

questions.stem: Six dots are drawn as three close pairs, and people see three groups rather than six dots. Which Gestalt principle explains this?

options.why: Similarity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that look alike.
Figure and ground is the Gestalt principle that we organize a scene into an object that stands out and its background.
Closure is the Gestalt principle that we fill in gaps to see a complete, whole object.
Correct. Proximity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that are near each other.

questions.explanation: Proximity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that are near each other.

questions.stem: A patient with amnesia cannot remember practicing a puzzle, yet he solves it faster each day. Which kind of memory is still working?

options.why: Correct. Implicit memory is the memory of skills and learned associations that is retained without conscious recall.
Phonemic encoding is the encoding of a word based on its sound.
Effortful processing is the encoding that requires attention and conscious effort.
Structural encoding is the shallow encoding of a word based on its appearance.

questions.explanation: Implicit memory is the memory of skills and learned associations that is retained without conscious recall.

questions.stem: Maya believes her grades depend entirely on how hard she works. Which belief does she hold?

options.why: Correct. An internal locus of control is the belief that a person controls their own outcomes through their own actions.
Downward social comparison is the comparing of oneself with people who are doing worse.
Upward social comparison is the comparing of oneself with people who are doing better.
The mere exposure effect is the tendency to like something more simply because we have encountered it repeatedly.

questions.explanation: An internal locus of control is the belief that a person controls their own outcomes through their own actions.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes grammar?

options.text: The whole system of rules in a language that lets people communicate
options.why: Correct. This is what grammar means.

options.text: The smallest distinctive unit of sound in a language
options.why: That describes a phoneme.

options.text: The rules for ordering words into sentences
options.why: That describes syntax.

options.text: The rules by which we get meaning from words and sentences
options.why: That describes semantics.

questions.explanation: Grammar is the whole system of rules in a language that lets people communicate.

questions.stem: The meditation group had lower cortisol levels. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: The daily activity and stress are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

options.text: The daily activity caused the difference in stress
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: An elderly woman's memory steadily worsens over several years until she no longer recognizes her family. Which condition does she most likely have?

options.why: Infantile amnesia is the inability of adults to remember events from the first few years of life.
Retrograde amnesia is the loss of memories from before an injury or illness.
Anterograde amnesia is the inability to form new memories after an injury or illness.
Correct. Alzheimer's disease is a progressive brain disease that destroys memory and then other mental abilities.

questions.explanation: Alzheimer's disease is a progressive brain disease that destroys memory and then other mental abilities.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the number of sound waves per second, which determines pitch?

options.why: Correct. Frequency is the number of sound waves per second, which determines pitch.
Amplitude is the height of a sound wave, which determines loudness.
Wavelength is the distance from one wave peak to the next, which determines the hue of light.
The cochlea is the coiled, fluid-filled tube in the inner ear where sound waves become neural impulses.

questions.explanation: Frequency is the number of sound waves per second, which determines pitch.

questions.stem: When the intelligence scores of a large population are graphed, they form a symmetrical bell shape. What is this shape called?

options.why: The mean is the arithmetic average of a set of scores.
Correct. The normal curve is the symmetrical, bell-shaped distribution in which most scores fall near the mean.
A percentile rank is the percentage of scores in a distribution that fall at or below a given score.
The range is the difference between the highest and lowest scores.

questions.explanation: The normal curve is the symmetrical, bell-shaped distribution in which most scores fall near the mean.

questions.stem: Positive psychologists group love, kindness and social intelligence under which virtue?

options.why: Justice is the category of character strengths that includes teamwork, fairness and leadership.
Correct. Humanity is the category of character strengths that includes love, kindness and social intelligence.
Courage is the category of character strengths that includes bravery, honesty and perseverance.
Temperance is the category of character strengths that includes forgiveness, humility and self-control.

questions.explanation: Humanity is the category of character strengths that includes love, kindness and social intelligence.

questions.stem: Which part of a neuron first receives a chemical message from a neighboring neuron?

options.why: The axon is the long fiber that carries the neural impulse away from the cell body toward other cells.
The axon terminals is the endings of the axon that release neurotransmitters.
The synapse is the tiny gap between the sending neuron and the receiving neuron.
Correct. A dendrite is a branching extension of a neuron that receives messages from other neurons.

questions.explanation: A dendrite is a branching extension of a neuron that receives messages from other neurons.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes Cluster A?

options.text: A lasting, rigid pattern of behavior and inner experience that differs from cultural expectations and impairs functioning
options.why: That describes a personality disorder.

options.text: The group of personality disorders marked by dramatic, emotional or erratic behavior: antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic
options.why: That describes Cluster B.

options.text: The group of personality disorders marked by anxious or fearful behavior: avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive
options.why: That describes Cluster C.

options.text: The group of personality disorders marked by odd or eccentric behavior: paranoid, schizoid and schizotypal
options.why: Correct. This is what Cluster A means.

questions.explanation: Cluster A is the group of personality disorders marked by odd or eccentric behavior: paranoid, schizoid and schizotypal.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the schedule in which the first response after an unpredictable amount of time is reinforced?

options.why: A variable-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after an unpredictable number of responses.
Correct. A variable-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after an unpredictable amount of time is reinforced.
A fixed-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after a set amount of time is reinforced.
Continuous reinforcement is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced every time it occurs.

questions.explanation: A variable-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after an unpredictable amount of time is reinforced.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the directionality problem in this study?

options.text: It is unclear whether the two measures were recorded
options.why: Both measures were recorded.

options.text: It is unclear whether the first measure influences the second or the second influences the first
options.why: Correct. A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

options.text: It is unclear whether the correlation is positive or negative
options.why: The sign of r shows the direction of the relationship.

options.text: It is unclear how many people took part
options.why: The sample size is stated.

questions.explanation: A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes fine motor skills?

options.text: The movements that use large muscles, such as crawling, walking and jumping
options.why: That describes gross motor skills.

options.text: The process by which some animals form a strong attachment to the first moving object they see
options.why: That describes imprinting.

options.text: A limited time early in life when certain experiences must occur for normal development
options.why: That describes a critical period.

options.text: The movements that use small muscles, such as grasping a crayon or buttoning a shirt
options.why: Correct. This is what fine motor skills means.

questions.explanation: Fine motor skills is the movements that use small muscles, such as grasping a crayon or buttoning a shirt.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes deinstitutionalization?

options.text: The movement, begun in the 1950s, of patients out of psychiatric hospitals and into community care
options.why: Correct. This is what deinstitutionalization means.

options.text: The choosing of treatments on the basis of research, clinical skill and the client's own values
options.why: That describes evidence-based practice.

options.text: The bond of trust and cooperation between therapist and client
options.why: That describes the therapeutic alliance.

options.text: A statistical procedure that combines the results of many studies to reach an overall conclusion
options.why: That describes a meta-analysis.

questions.explanation: Deinstitutionalization is the movement, begun in the 1950s, of patients out of psychiatric hospitals and into community care.

questions.stem: A theory says that neurons alternate firing, like soldiers taking turns shooting, to keep up with sounds faster than one neuron can fire. Which theory is this?

options.why: Sensorineural deafness is hearing loss caused by damage to the hair cells of the cochlea or to the auditory nerve.
Place theory is the theory that we hear different pitches because different sound waves trigger different places on the cochlea's membrane.
Correct. Volley theory is the theory that groups of neurons take turns firing so that together they match high sound frequencies.
Sound localization is the ability to tell where a sound comes from, using differences in timing and loudness between the two ears.

questions.explanation: Volley theory is the theory that groups of neurons take turns firing so that together they match high sound frequencies.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the participants to the two conditions at random?

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

That is an in-depth study of one individual.
That is explaining the study to participants afterward.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: As Pia brings a pencil toward her nose, her eyes turn inward, and her brain uses the muscle strain to judge the distance. Which depth cue is this?

options.why: Interposition is the monocular depth cue in which an object that partly blocks another is seen as closer.
Retinal disparity is the binocular depth cue based on the difference between the images in the two eyes.
Correct. Convergence is the binocular depth cue based on how far the eyes turn inward to focus on a near object.
Linear perspective is the monocular depth cue in which parallel lines seem to meet in the distance.

questions.explanation: Convergence is the binocular depth cue based on how far the eyes turn inward to focus on a near object.

questions.stem: A questionnaire tells Ravi that his top character traits are curiosity, fairness and humor, and encourages him to use them daily. These traits are called which of the following?

options.why: Resilience is the ability to recover and adapt well after stress or hardship.
Correct. Signature strengths is the positive character traits, such as kindness or curiosity, that are most central to a particular person.
Posttraumatic growth is the positive psychological change that some people experience after struggling with a very difficult event.
Positive psychology is the scientific study of the strengths and conditions that help people and communities thrive.

questions.explanation: Signature strengths is the positive character traits, such as kindness or curiosity, that are most central to a particular person.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the base of the brainstem, which controls heartbeat and breathing?

options.why: The pituitary gland is the master gland of the endocrine system, which is controlled by the hypothalamus.
The reticular activating system is the network of neurons in the brainstem that controls arousal and alertness.
The cerebellum is the structure at the back of the brainstem that coordinates balance, movement and procedural learning.
Correct. The medulla is the base of the brainstem, which controls heartbeat and breathing.

questions.explanation: The medulla is the base of the brainstem, which controls heartbeat and breathing.

questions.stem: A patient with damage to the visual cortex says she sees nothing, yet she walks around obstacles in a hallway. Which condition does she have?

options.why: Correct. Blindsight is the ability to respond to visual information without consciously seeing it.
Dichromatism is a form of color vision deficiency in which one of the three types of cones does not work.
Prosopagnosia is the inability to recognize faces, even familiar ones, after brain damage.
Monochromatism is a rare form of color blindness in which a person sees only shades of gray.

questions.explanation: Blindsight is the ability to respond to visual information without consciously seeing it.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the operational definition of the dependent variable?

questions.stem: Jamal reads a phone number and can hold it in mind for about twenty seconds before it fades. Which memory store is he using?

options.why: Long-term memory is the relatively permanent and limitless store of knowledge, skills and experiences.
Echoic memory is the sensory memory of a sound, which lasts three or four seconds.
Correct. Short-term memory is the memory store that briefly holds a few items, about seven, before they are stored or forgotten.
Iconic memory is the brief sensory memory of a visual image, which lasts a few tenths of a second.

questions.explanation: Short-term memory is the memory store that briefly holds a few items, about seven, before they are stored or forgotten.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes narcolepsy?

options.text: A sleep disorder in which breathing repeatedly stops during sleep, causing brief awakenings
options.why: That describes sleep apnea.

options.text: Sleepwalking, which occurs during deep NREM sleep

options.why: Correct. This is what narcolepsy means.

questions.explanation: Narcolepsy is a sleep disorder with sudden, uncontrollable attacks of sleep, often straight into REM sleep.

questions.stem: After two years of long hours and constant pressure, a nurse feels drained, detached and ineffective. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: An industrial-organizational psychologist is a psychologist who studies behavior in the workplace to improve productivity and well-being.
Correct. Burnout is the physical and emotional exhaustion that results from long-term stress at work.
The bystander effect is the tendency for a person to be less likely to help when other people are present.

questions.explanation: Burnout is the physical and emotional exhaustion that results from long-term stress at work.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes respect for people's rights and dignity?

questions.stem: After Mia talks back, her mother gives her extra chores, and she talks back less often. Being given the chores is an example of which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Positive punishment is the weakening of a behavior by adding an unpleasant stimulus after it.
Negative punishment is the weakening of a behavior by removing a pleasant stimulus after it.
Negative reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by removing an unpleasant stimulus after it.

questions.explanation: Positive punishment is the weakening of a behavior by adding an unpleasant stimulus after it.

questions.stem: An eight-month-old learns about a rattle by shaking it, looking at it and putting it in her mouth. Which of Piaget's stages is she in?

options.why: The preoperational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 2 to 7, in which children use words and images but cannot yet reason logically.
The concrete operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 7 to 11, in which children think logically about real objects and events.
Correct. The sensorimotor stage is Piaget's stage from birth to about age 2, in which infants know the world through senses and actions.
The formal operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 12 on, in which people can reason about abstract and hypothetical ideas.

questions.explanation: The sensorimotor stage is Piaget's stage from birth to about age 2, in which infants know the world through senses and actions.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes massed practice?

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the influence that comes from a person's willingness to accept others' views as evidence about reality?

Normative social influence is the influence that comes from a person's desire to gain approval or avoid rejection.

The peripheral route to persuasion is persuasion that works through surface cues, such as an attractive or famous speaker.

questions.explanation: Informational social influence is the influence that comes from a person's willingness to accept others' views as evidence about reality.

options.why: A pessimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as lasting, affecting everything and caused by oneself.

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of the severity of depression

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of the severity of depression.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: The severity of depression was defined as each participant's score on a standard depression questionnaire after twelve weeks.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The therapy group had lower depression scores. On average, the value was 11 for the group that received therapy and 21 for the group on the waiting list, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent: participants agreed to take part after being told about the study. (Also acceptable: debriefing; the right to withdraw; approval by an institutional review board.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 90 adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The therapy group had lower depression scores. (11 compared with 21).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that the treatment affects the severity of depression. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to the treatment. The finding illustrates cognitive-behavioral therapy, which reduces depression by changing negative thought patterns (the cognitive triad) and behavior.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: How does long-term stress affect health, and what reduces its effects?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Long-term stress harms health, but coping strategies and social support reduce its effects.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source A, people with more stressful life events had more colds in the same year (r = +0.33).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through the general adaptation syndrome: prolonged stress keeps the body in the resistance phase and eventually exhausts it, which suppresses the immune system and makes illness more likely.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, workers who practiced mindfulness meditation had lower cortisol levels (9.8) than workers who listened to an audiobook (13.5).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through emotion-focused coping: meditation manages the emotional and physical reaction to stress, which lowers the body's stress-hormone response.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
